label: Clinical Documentation Assistant
description: Draft high-quality clinical documents — discharge summaries, referral letters, outpatient letters, clinical notes — to professional standards. Adapts to specialty, setting, and local documentation requirements. Saves clinicians significant administrative time while maintaining medico-legal accuracy.

claudeKnowledge.description: Clinical documentation standards, SBAR framework, SOAP notes, NHS discharge summary requirements, referral letter etiquette, medico-legal documentation, specialty-specific formats

guidedInputs.label: Clinical Details
guidedInputs.placeholder: Paste your clinical notes, bullet points, or key facts. Include: presenting complaint, relevant history, examination findings, investigations, diagnosis, management, follow-up plan. The richer your input, the better the output.

guidedInputs.label: Patient Demographics (optional)
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. 67-year-old female, type 2 diabetic, hypertensive — no identifiable information needed

guidedInputs.label: Tone / Format Notes
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Concise — max 1 page. Include medications table. Use SBAR format.

exampleInput: Draft a discharge summary for the GP from these notes: 67-year-old female admitted with community-acquired pneumonia (CURB-65 score 2). Treated with IV co-amoxiclav for 48 hours then stepped down to oral. Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe consolidation, no effusion. Background of type 2 diabetes (metformin) and hypertension (ramipril). Day 3: afebrile, oxygen weaned, mobilising independently. Discharged day 5 with three further days of oral antibiotics. Plan: repeat chest X-ray in 6 weeks to confirm resolution; GP to review blood pressure — systolic readings ran in the 150s throughout admission.

exampleValues.clinical_context: 67F admitted with CAP (CURB-65 = 2). IV co-amoxiclav 48h then stepped down to oral. CXR: right lower lobe consolidation, no effusion. PMH: T2DM (metformin 500 mg BD), hypertension (ramipril 5 mg OD). Day 3: afebrile, SpO2 95% on room air, mobilising. Discharged day 5 with 3 further days oral co-amoxiclav. Plan: repeat CXR in 6 weeks; GP to review BP (systolic 150s during admission).
exampleValues.tone_notes: Concise — max 1 page. Include medications table.
